title: Authority: Directed Deference
coreMove: Verify whether the authority signal is genuine and qualified for this exact choice.
sourcePressure: The source narrowly supports deference to rank, expertise, legitimacy, titles, uniforms, symbols, and status cues, with defense focused on whether the authority is real, relevant, and earned for the decision.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not write an anti-expert chapter; the issue is authority cues outrunning relevance.

hook: The badge is not the answer

exampleSpecs.audience: a homeowner weighing advice from a confident inspector
exampleSpecs.stakes: paying for unnecessary window replacements because the title feels decisive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the homeowner asks which code section applies to these exact windows instead of accepting the inspector's title alone
exampleSpecs.firstImage: peeling sash paint collected on a folded permit notice

exampleSpecs.audience: a beginner aquarist hearing advice from a staff member in a branded vest
exampleSpecs.stakes: buying incompatible equipment because the uniform signals expertise
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the buyer asks the staffer to match each item to the tank's volume and species list before checkout
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a refractometer case beside bags of live sand

exampleSpecs.audience: a first-generation student facing a senior administrator
exampleSpecs.stakes: accepting an appeal denial without checking policy fit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the student reads the policy paragraph aloud and asks the administrator to show where her case fails it
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a financial aid folder held shut with a bent paper clip

exampleSpecs.audience: a host buying bottles for a retirement dinner
exampleSpecs.stakes: choosing a costly bottle because a framed certificate sits behind the register
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the host notices the certificate, then asks how the recommended bottle fits the menu and guest preferences
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a cream label tilted in a wooden display rack

exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer approving a safety shortcut from a founding member
exampleSpecs.stakes: letting status override the machine's posted procedure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a scorched test piece, the volunteer traces the shortcut back to founding-member status rather than relevant safety knowledge
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a square of scorched plywood under the cutter lid

exampleSpecs.domain: independent lab report for well water
exampleSpecs.audience: a rural property buyer reading advice from a real estate agent
exampleSpecs.stakes: skipping a second test because the agent sounds authoritative outside her domain
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the buyer separates the agent's market expertise from water safety expertise and orders the lab retest
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a capped sample bottle in a zippered plastic bag

skillTargets: distinguish legitimate expertise from authority appearance
test relevance of a credential to the decision
identify rank cues that are outside their domain

tryThisNowSpec: For one authoritative recommendation today, ask what exact expertise would be needed to answer this decision and whether the speaker has that expertise.
